response.sql:
WITH type_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    e.type,
    AVG(b.spent / b.amount) as avg_ratio
  FROM event e
  JOIN budget b ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event
  WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL 
    AND b.amount IS NOT NULL 
    AND b.amount != 0
  GROUP BY e.type
),
mean_ratio AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as overall_mean
  FROM type_ratios
)
SELECT 
  tr.type,
  tr.avg_ratio,
  mr.overall_mean,
  tr.avg_ratio - mr.overall_mean as deviation_from_mean
FROM type_ratios tr
CROSS JOIN mean_ratio mr
ORDER BY tr.type;

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines with amount = 0 are excluded to avoid division by zero; NULL values in spent or amount are excluded per standard SQL AVG() semantics.

The average is computed across individual budget line ratios per event type, then the mean is taken across event types. This differs from computing one ratio per type from aggregated spent/amount totals.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute the aggregate spent-to-budgeted ratio per event type (sum of all spent divided by sum of all budgeted) rather than averaging individual line ratios, then show deviation from the mean of those aggregate ratios.
alternatives.sql:
WITH type_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    e.type,
    SUM(b.spent) / SUM(b.amount) as aggregate_ratio
  FROM event e
  JOIN budget b ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event
  WHERE b.spent IS NOT NULL 
    AND b.amount IS NOT NULL 
    AND b.amount > 0
  GROUP BY e.type
),
mean_ratio AS (
  SELECT AVG(aggregate_ratio) as overall_mean
  FROM type_ratios
)
SELECT 
  tr.type,
  tr.aggregate_ratio,
  mr.overall_mean,
  tr.aggregate_ratio - mr.overall_mean as deviation_from_mean
FROM type_ratios tr
CROSS JOIN mean_ratio mr
ORDER BY tr.type;
